title: Two pointers and sliding windows
summary: Walk through an array with two indexes at once to replace a slow loop-inside-a-loop with a single pass.

sections.heading: Two pointers from both ends
body: On a **sorted** array, start one pointer at each end. If the pair is too small, move the left one right (bigger numbers). If it is too big, move the right one left. Each step rules out a whole row of pairs, so it takes one pass instead of checking every pair.

sections.heading: A window of fixed size
body: For "the best run of `k` items in a row", do not add up every window from scratch. Slide it: add the item that enters on the right and subtract the one that leaves on the left.

python.code:
def max_window_sum(nums, k):
    total = sum(nums[:k])
    best = total
    for i in range(k, len(nums)):
        total += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
        best = max(best, total)
    return best

print(max_window_sum([2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2], 3))

sections.heading: A window that grows and shrinks
body: Sometimes the window size is the answer. Example: the longest stretch of text with no repeated letter.

Move `end` forward one character at a time. When the new character already appears inside the window, jump `start` just past its last position. The window is always valid, and each pointer only moves forward, so it is still one pass.

mistakes: Using the two-ends trick on an array that is not sorted.
Moving `start` backwards: only move it forward (`prev >= start`).
Off-by-one in the window length: it is `end - start + 1`.
